Posted March 5, 2003
Analysis by Richard Cowan

The Canadian government's eight day refugee board hearings for Steve Kubby and his family began today with a crucial concession from the Canadian government.

In his brief opening statement, the representative of the Immigration Minister did not assert the absolute doctrine that there could be no refugees from DEAland, as has previously been argued by the government and a prohibitionist local Member of Parliament, Randy White.

Instead, after asserting that DEAland is a democratic country with a system of checks and balances, etc., the Immigration official simply said that a claimant must meet a very high onus to prove their case. That is something that the Kubbys can certainly meet.

This is an enormously important concession. Had the government simply asserted that there can be no refugees from the Leader of the Free World, then the Kubbys and the other claimants would be in the position of asking the Refugee Protection people to challenge the fundamental policies of the Canadian government.

Of course, I suspect that the Canadian officials simply cannot imagine the depth of corruption in DEAland law enforcement, so they may not understand the significance of this concession.

The Kubbys lead witness is California journalist, Pat McCartney, formerly of the Auburn Journal, where he covered much of the Kubby trial.
See
Local Editor Says Kubby Prosecution Ends with a Whimper.
and
How Much More Will Bad law Enforcement Cost the Taxpayers of California?
Learning to Take Human Rights Seriously
 Or Why Dehumanizing People Is An Expensive Delusion
and links

As it happens, McCartney was so appalled by what he saw in Placer County, and by what the papers would not let him report, that he quit and is now researching a book on how California and federal law enforcement conspired to thwart the will of the people of California, even breaking the law in the process.

McCartney has used the California Public Documents Act to get access to the records of meetings attended by former California Attorney General Lundgren and other officials in which they were very brazen in their efforts. These people are so arrogant that they did not bother to hide what they were doing.

Often, even their public statements revealed their contempt for the very laws that they were sworn to uphold.

McCartney has also sought federal documents under the Freedom of Information Act, which Attorney General Ashcroft has sought to eviscerate, so that it is more difficult to uncover his war against the Constitution.

His book, which will be published next year, is going to be a bombshell in the medical cannabis debate, and in California politics. McCartney explained to the hearings that the criminal justice system in DEAland no longer works as the Canadian government assumes, because of the Drug War, and especially in medical cannabis cases.

McCartney's testimony and that of some of the other witnesses for the Kubbys will also be relevant for Steve Tuck and Ken Hayes. Hayes hearing is in April and Tuck's is in May.
See
Confusion Over Medical Cannabis in Canada Reflected in Immigration Hearings. Defense Fund For Steve Tuck to Be Organized. Special to MarijuanaNews

Heretofore, I had just assumed that they would lose at the hearings and have to appeal to the Canadian courts. It now seems possible that they will prevail in their refugee claims at the basic level.

Today's subtle shift in the Canadian government's position is also important beyond these three cases. Little by little, cannabis prohibition, especially as enforced in DEAland is being put on trial.

In the meantime, the Canadian Supreme Court will be hearing constitutional challenges to all of Canada's laws, and there are several appeals working their way through the Canadian courts on medical cannabis, as well.
See
Canadian Supreme Court Punts On Cannabis Cases Until Spring. The Games Governments Play Prove The Need for International Debate on Cannabis Prohibition. Special to MarijuanaNews

Cannabis prohibition is practically and philosophically incompatible with the Canadian system of justice, that is good for my friends here and good for the friends of freedom everywhere.
See
Canadian Prime Minister Says He Has Been In Favor Of Decrim Since 1980. How Time Flies When You Are In Power. Possession Law Hostage to Medical Cannabis. Another Deadline On Taking Care of Patients.
